Question
========
What are the techniques used by GPUs to hide memory latency?


Answerlist
----------
* Less level of caches
* High memory bandwidth
* Hardware-based context switches between threads
* Speculative execution
* RT cores
* Just-in-time compilation

Solution
========
A GPU does not try to make a single memory access fast. It keeps a very large number of threads resident and switches between them in hardware at no cost, so that whenever a warp stalls on memory another one is ready to run. This is backed by very wide, high bandwidth memory.

Answerlist
----------
* 0. Having fewer cache levels does not hide latency, it exposes it.
* 1. Wide, high bandwidth memory lets many outstanding requests be served in parallel.
* 1. Zero-cost hardware switching between resident warps keeps the execution units busy while others wait on memory.
* 0. This is a latency hiding technique of large out-of-order CPUs, not of GPUs.
* 0. Ray tracing units are fixed function accelerators, unrelated to memory latency.
* 0. Compilation happens before execution and does not hide memory latency at run time.
